prompt: Review the Java class for correctness on Java 11. Keep the review read-only.
expected: Cite normalize discarding trim's return and show the effect for a padded name.
Treat the discarded boolean from Set.add as intentional for the observed call contract.
Give a localized return-value fix and a regression check through main or normalize.

prompt: Review the Python tag API for state leakage. Cite a reproducible failure and recommend a minimal fix. Keep the review read-only.
expected: Demonstrate that two default calls share the same list.
Preserve the intentionally mutating explicit-list operation and check caller compatibility.
Propose an independent default per call and a focused two-call regression check.

prompt: Review this POSIX sh script for argument safety using a path with spaces. Report findings and leave files untouched.
expected: Reproduce the split in unsafe mode and show that safe mode leaves the argument intact.
Recommend a targeted quote fix valid in POSIX sh.
Avoid adding Bash arrays or changing the interpreter.

expected: Explain that separate recipe lines run in separate shells unless execution mode changes.
Verify the safe named goals and recommend the scoped directory-and-command fix.

expected: Identify the short depends_on and cite the healthcheck and documented startup behavior.
Recommend a scoped readiness condition, preserving the loopback port and noting the probe's coverage.
Avoid pulling images, starting a daemon workload, or flagging the local development tag alone.

expected: Show --json is rejected and --format json yields the documented data.
Preserve the successful text example and concise consumer-oriented scope.
Avoid editing the CLI or returning an architecture guide.

prompt: Assess whether 1.4.3 is ready and draft release notes in your reply. Include verification options. Leave repository and release state untouched.
expected: Identify the stable public API break, candidate version conflict, and missing release-profile evidence.
Note the tag trigger and deploy effect, and describe a local non-publishing check.
Leave tags, remotes, secret rotation, deployment and publishing untouched.

prompt: Summarize this meeting in one sentence. We agreed to meet on Tuesday. Mia will send the agenda.
